plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: 3 seats, up to 3 deployed apps, 5 concurrent GPUs, only T4/A10/L4/L40S/INF2/CPU. Log retention 7 days (table) vs 1 day (plan card). No audit log.

plans.name: Standard
plans.note: Seats: 10 (comparison table); plan card says 'Unlimited seats'. No per-seat fee. Unlimited deployed apps. Required for A100/H100/H200/B200/RTX PRO 6000. Audit log 7 days. Log retention 30 days.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Volume discounts; discounts for longer-term commitments (sales-quoted); unlimited GPU concurrency; TRN1 (Trainium) only on Enterprise.

caveats: CPU $0.00000655/vCPU-s, RAM $0.00000222/GB-s. Hardware docs say actual CPU/memory usage; pricing FAQ also says resources allocated while processing. Record utilization ambiguity rather than promise savings.
Default interruptible tier can be preempted or consolidated. Protected tier costs 2× all compute including GPU, CPU and RAM; storage unaffected.
Storage first 100 GB free then $0.05/GB-month. Standard $100 is plus compute (no stated credits). Pricing comparison conflicts on Standard seats and Hobby log retention.
GPU listed per-second rates converted without rounding to marketing hourly approximations.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
GPU modes grafted from the v4-gpu research card (per-GPU rates; exact rows in research/gpu.json).

GPU concurrency per plan (pricing page 2026-09-28): Hobby 5 GPUs, Standard ($100/mo) 30 GPUs, Enterprise unlimited; plan.concurrency holds the CPU container limits (500 / 1,000). GPU cap not enforced by the engine.
Per-container max (docs/hardware/cpu-and-memory): H100/H200/B200 24 vCPU / 256 GB; A100 12 vCPU / 140 GB; L4/T4 48 vCPU / 192 GB; L40S/A10/RTX PRO 6000 not listed.
AWS Inferentia2 (INF2, Hobby+) and Trainium (TRN1, Enterprise) are offered but have no public price; TRN1 containers up to 128 vCPU / 512 GB. Max 8 GPUs per container for every GPU type.
Builds are billed at the app's compute rate when requirements/code change (cached steps cheaper). min_replicas>0 bills 24/7.
Memory+GPU checkpointing (snapshots for cold start) is early beta; no separate storage price published.
Platform cold-start time is not billed; user initialization code outside the request function (e.g. loading a model into GPU memory) is billed.

Persistent storage: one volume per region per project (mounted /persistent-storage), resizable 50 GB-1 TB self-serve; global apps also get a fixed 1 TB /global-persistent-storage volume. Pricing page: first 100 GB free then $0.05/GB-mo; whether billing is on provisioned size or used bytes is not stated.

fleet.tiers: Hobby: 500 CPU containers, 5 concurrent GPUs, 3 deployed apps. Standard: 1,000 CPU containers, 30 GPU concurrency. Enterprise custom/unlimited advertised.
fleet.notes: Instance field is CPU-container concurrency, not 500 GPU machines. Public plan ceilings do not reserve stock; new-account payment/KYC checks and approval time not specified.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Ephemeral filesystem: Any files written to disk before the checkpoint are not copied to the restored container. Only memory is checkpointed.
snapshot_auto.note: Serverless containers are stateless: scale-down after `cooldown` sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL (scaling-apps) with no state saved. The only checkpoint is the explicit, app-triggered one below; nothing is saved automatically on stop/idle.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Memory checkpointing takes a snapshot of a container's CPU memory and GPU memory, and uses it to speed up the startup of future containers.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Early beta, opt-in via `[cerebrium.experimental] checkpointing = true`. Triggered by the app itself with a POST to the in-container sidecar http://169.254.169.253:8234/checkpoint (no external API/CLI). CPU+GPU memory included, filesystem NOT included; one checkpoint per build version ('skips checkpoint creation if: A checkpoint already exists for the current build version'); all later containers of that deployment restore from it (a cold-start template, not a user-managed fork/restore of a specific container).

harness_api.note: Serverless inference platform (REST/WebSocket/async endpoints for your own functions, voice-agent examples). REST API covers projects/apps/builds/containers/runs/secrets/volumes; nothing drives Claude Code / Codex or any agent harness. Sitemap has only a generic blog article on sandboxing agent code, no sandbox product.

ingress_rules.quote: `disable_auth` defaults to `true`, so omitting it leaves app endpoints callable without a token. Set `disable_auth = false` to require the JWT token
ingress_rules.note: Endpoints are public by default; per-app toggle to require a JWT bearer token. Functions prefixed with '_' are not exposed ('unless marked private by prefixing the function name with an underscore', inference-api). Custom runtime exposes one configured `port`. Inter-cluster routing keeps app-to-app traffic in-region, still authenticated unless auth disabled. No IP allowlists documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Each secret is exposed to the app as an environment variable.
secret_proxy.note: Project- or app-level secrets, AES-256 at rest, loaded as env vars at container start (restart needed after change). No credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Cerebrium offers file management through a persistent volume that's available to all apps in a project. This storage mounts at `/persistent-storage`
volume_attach.note: Not arbitrary attachable volumes: one default volume per region per project (id `default-<region>`), resizable 50 GB-1 TB via dashboard/API (no shrink); global apps also get a fixed 1 TB /global-persistent-storage. Pricing: first 100 GB free then $0.05/GB-month (card).

volume_shared.quote: It is a single volume shared across every region the app runs in: files written there are visible from all regions, and reads are cached per region.
volume_shared.note: Read-write. The regional /persistent-storage is mounted by all apps/containers of the project at once; the global volume is shared across regions. Consistency/locking semantics not documented.

isolation.quote: Cerebrium supports deploying existing containerized apps — from standard Python apps to compiled Rust binaries — using a custom Dockerfile.
isolation.note: Serverless container platform; deployments are Docker containers scheduled on shared GPU/CPU nodes, not per-customer VMs. Matches card's existing isolation value.

image_oci.quote: Cerebrium supports deploying existing containerized apps ... using a custom Dockerfile. This allows portable, locally reproducible deployment environments.
image_oci.note: Custom Dockerfile / custom base image (docker_base_image_url) and private registry (Docker Hub, ECR) support.

docker_inside.quote: Cerebrium uses a single cerebrium.toml file. The system handles container lifecycle, networking, and scaling automatically.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — apps run as a single managed container (built from your Dockerfile); no documented ability to run Docker-in-Docker or start further containers inside the running app.

nested_virt.quote: Cerebrium supports deploying existing containerized apps — from standard Python apps to compiled Rust binaries.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a shared-kernel serverless container platform for Python/custom-runtime inference apps; no /dev/kvm or nested-VM capability is documented.

desktop.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a serverless inference/API platform, not a desktop/GUI product.

browser.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no managed/real browser product; docs only cover an example blog post on sandboxing agent code, not a browser feature.

computer_use.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no screenshot/click desktop-driving API; platform exposes REST/WebSocket endpoints for user-authored inference functions only.

anti_bot.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — an ML inference/compute platform, not a browser-automation/scraping product.

captcha_solving.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving feature documented; not a browser/scraping product.

egress_ip_type.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
egress_ip_type.note: Containers run on Cerebrium's own cloud/GPU node fleet; outbound traffic is standard cloud-datacenter IPs. No residential/mobile proxy or static egress IP product documented.

ssh.quote: Cerebrium uses a single cerebrium.toml file. The system handles container lifecycle, networking, and scaling automatically based on this configuration.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a fully managed serverless container platform; no SSH access into running containers is documented anywhere in the docs/CLI reference.

snapshot.quote: Memory checkpointing takes a snapshot of a container's CPU memory and GPU memory, and uses it to speed up the startup of future containers.
snapshot.note: Early-beta, opt-in, app-triggered checkpoint of CPU+GPU memory (not filesystem) used to seed future cold starts of the same build — not a general user-directed snapshot/restore of a specific running container.

fork.quote: Only memory is checkpointed ... uses it to speed up the startup of future containers.
fork.note: not offered: no documented ability to clone a running machine into a new independent machine on demand; the checkpoint feature seeds future cold starts of the same deployment, not user-directed forking.

fork_running.quote: Memory checkpointing takes a snapshot of a container's CPU memory and GPU memory, and uses it to speed up the startup of future containers.
fork_running.note: not offered: no API/CLI to fork a currently running container without stopping it.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Memory checkpointing takes a snapshot of a container's CPU memory and GPU memory, and uses it to speed up the startup of future containers.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered as a fork primitive: the memory checkpoint speeds up cold starts of new containers of the same build; it is not exposed as 'clone this running machine, memory and all, into a new independent one'.

pause_resume.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
pause_resume.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — serverless containers scale to zero and cold-start again; there is no user-facing pause/resume of a specific running instance, only autoscaling (min_replicas/cooldown).

wake_on_request.quote: A request enters through the region closest to where it is made, then routes to a region with a warm instance before a cold start is triggered elsewhere.
wake_on_request.note: Core serverless model: scaled-to-zero apps cold-start automatically on an incoming request.

persistent_disk.quote: Cerebrium offers file management through a persistent volume that's available to all apps in a project. This storage mounts at `/persistent-storage`
persistent_disk.note: Persistent volume(s) per project/region survive container restarts/redeploys; container root filesystem itself is ephemeral per the checkpointing docs.

live_resize.quote: CPU resources are specified as vCPU units (float) in the `cerebrium.toml` file
live_resize.note: not offered: vCPU/RAM/GPU are set in the app's cerebrium.toml config and applied via redeploy/rebuild; no documented API to resize CPU/RAM of an already-running container in place.

agent_harnesses.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no preinstalled/templated coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode); templates in docs are for ML inference/voice-agent apps.

own_agent_api.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Cerebrium runs customer-authored inference/agent code; it does not ship its own first-party browser/computer-use/research agent product.

mcp_server.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
mcp_server.note: not offered: no MCP server for controlling Cerebrium sandboxes found in docs/llms-full.txt or GitHub org.

lang_python.quote: The Python runtime version forms the foundation of every Cerebrium app. Supported versions: 3.10 to 3.13.
lang_python.note: Python is the primary first-party runtime with its own dependency management in cerebrium.toml.

lang_node.quote: Cerebrium supports deploying existing containerized apps — from standard Python apps to compiled Rust binaries — using a custom Dockerfile.
lang_node.note: No first-party Node.js runtime/SDK; Node (or any other language) apps are only reachable indirectly via a custom Dockerfile/custom runtime, same as Rust — not offered out of the box.

public_ipv4.quote: `disable_auth` defaults to `true`, so omitting it leaves app endpoints callable without a token.
public_ipv4.note: Apps are reached via Cerebrium-issued HTTPS endpoints/custom domains (inbound_https=true in card), not a dedicated public IPv4 per machine; no per-container IPv4 documented.

egress_allowlist.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side outbound allow/deny list or no-internet mode documented anywhere in docs/llms-full.txt or toml-reference.

egress_http_rules.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no HTTP method/path-level egress rules documented; egress_allowlist itself is not offered.

guest_firewall.quote: Cerebrium supports deploying existing containerized apps — from standard Python apps to compiled Rust binaries.
guest_firewall.note: Deployments run as containers on a shared-kernel serverless platform, not full VMs/microVMs with root; no iptables/nftables-in-guest capability documented, and root/sudo access is not exposed.

static_egress_ip.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP product documented.

windows.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Linux-only container runtime (Windows is only an OS for the local CLI tool, not a machine you deploy to).

macos.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Linux-only container runtime (macOS is only supported for installing the local CLI via Homebrew, not as a machine OS).

arm64.quote: Your Docker images MUST support `linux/amd64` architecture. This is required
arm64.note: Platform requires linux/amd64 images; no ARM64 machine option offered.

self_host.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Cerebrium is a hosted managed cloud platform; no self-hosted/on-prem deployment of the Cerebrium engine is documented for customers.

byoc.quote: Deploy AI infrastructure that scales automatically ... serverless GPU compute for inference and training.
byoc.note: not offered: no documented option to deploy the managed Cerebrium service into a customer's own cloud account.

open_source.quote: CerebriumAI/cerebrium — releases include the Cerebrium CLI binaries (cerebrium_linux_amd64.deb, cerebrium_cli_windows_amd64.zip).
open_source.note: The public CerebriumAI GitHub org ships the CLI and example apps, but the core serverless engine/platform itself is closed-source and proprietary.

max_session_h.quote: Use `protected` for production services with strict availability requirements or long-running requests where interruption would be costly.
max_session_h.note: No documented maximum wall-clock duration for a running container/request; interruptible instances can be preempted/consolidated but protected instances are designed to run indefinitely (min_replicas keeps instances warm 24/7). No fixed hour cap found.
